task: Escribe 130–160 palabras sobre tu experiencia aprendiendo inglés: qué te resultó más difícil, qué beneficios notaste y qué le recomendarías a otra persona. Usa el present perfect continuous.
paragraphs: Not so long ago, many parents and teachers believed that bringing up a child with two languages was a bad idea. It would confuse the child, they thought, and slow down their development. Today, bilingualism is more often described as a superpower. The truth, as usual, is more nuanced.

We now know that children are perfectly capable of learning two or more languages at the same time. Bilingual children may know fewer words in each individual language than monolingual children of the same age, but when both languages are counted together, their vocabulary is usually just as large. Mixing languages within a sentence, which once worried parents, is now seen as a natural and skilful use of both systems rather than a sign of confusion.

The more controversial question is whether bilingualism brings advantages beyond language itself. Since both languages are always active in the brain, bilingual people constantly have to select one and suppress the other. Some researchers proposed that this daily mental exercise strengthens "executive functions", the skills we use to focus, switch between tasks and ignore distractions. Early studies seemed to confirm this so-called bilingual advantage.

However, as more and larger studies were carried out, the picture became less clear. Several attempts to replicate the original findings failed, and some scientists now believe that the advantage, if it exists, is small and depends on many other factors, such as education, income and how often people actually switch between their languages.

Another much-discussed claim is that bilingualism may help to delay the symptoms of dementia in old age. Some studies have reported delays of several years, but others have found little or no effect, and the debate continues.

What is beyond doubt is that speaking another language opens doors: to other cultures, other people and other ways of seeing the world. Even if it does not turn us into geniuses, that may be reason enough to learn one.
